task: Extend the CI wiring guard past scripts/ci using reachability rather than literal reference (#3341)

events.content: Measured the issue's headline claim before writing anything
Classified all six remaining scripts individually
Wired the one candidate that passes clean
Wrote tests/ci/test_validation_scripts_are_reachable.py and it caught a defect in itself on first run
Fixed a pre-existing push blocker exposed by touching the workflow
Filed #3360 for the three validators that fail against the current tree

Stopped the reachability scan from reading comments and docstrings. It matched '<stem>.py' anywhere in the raw file, so prose manufactured reachability, which is the defect _strip_commented_lines already prevents on the workflow side. The scan now reads only non-docstring string literals, which is where a subprocess invocation actually names a script.

The stricter scan exposed two genuinely unwired scripts: validate_templates_schema.py, held up only by a yaml_loader.py docstring whose edge pointed from the library to its own consumer, and check_skill_portability.py, named only in two companion docstrings. Both exit 0, so both are wireable; filed #3366 and allowlisted them against it. Also corrected templates/README.md, which claimed the first runs in build-validation.yml, a workflow that no longer exists.

parse_agent_file crashed with a traceback on a non-UTF-8 file instead of reporting it. Same shape as the silent skip fixed earlier: the run ends without a usable validation result. UnicodeDecodeError and OSError now become MalformedAgentFileError, so the directory walk reports the file and keeps going.

Re-extracted the episode after the work-log additions. The extractor appends rather than rebuilds, so a corrected log does not correct an episode already on disk; the file has to be deleted first. Result: 11 events, no inherited content. Filed as #3363 separately, since the derived file should not need hand-holding.

Review caught two caps that had drifted apart: the spelled-out number table stopped at eight while the allowlist size test permitted twelve, so a ninth entry would have crashed the docstring check with a KeyError instead of reporting the stale docstring it exists to report. Both now read one constant, and a test pins the table to span it.

lessons: Measure the claim in an issue before implementing its remedy. The count was an artifact of asking about literal reference rather than reachability. Changing the question dropped it to six and made the allowlist small enough to be honest. Implementing the requested remedy directly would have reproduced the defect the issue was filed against.

Avoid: Trusting a new guard's first green or red run without probing the guard itself. Verify each reported violation by hand before accepting it, and keep a test class whose job is to guard the guard.
